hazard: Delays in patient handover causing ambulance resource unavailability

anchor.title: Frederick Pring: Prevention of Future Deaths Report
anchor.quote: the current practices in place for the handover of patients at an Emergency Department far too often results in wholly unacceptable delays with patients being kept waiting for long periods in ambulances and ambulance resources consequently being unavailable for allocation to other calls

members.title: Peter Scott
members.explanation: Both reports identify delayed patient handovers at emergency departments causing prolonged ambulance waits and reduced availability of ambulance resources as a safety risk.
members.earlier_quote: the current practices in place for the handover of patients at an Emergency Department far too often results in wholly unacceptable delays with patients being kept waiting for long periods in ambulances and ambulance resources consequently being unavailable for allocation to other calls.
members.later_quote: one of the key problems in ensuring ambulance availability is delayed handover of patients at hospitals.

members.title: Rebecca Evans
members.explanation: Both reports identify the same hazard: prolonged patient handover delays in the Emergency Department causing ambulance backlog and delayed care. The mechanism described—unacceptable delays keeping patients in ambulances and tying up resources—is unchanged.
members.earlier_quote: That the current practices in place for the handover of patients at an Emergency Department far too often results in wholly unacceptable delays with patients being kept waiting for long periods in ambulances
members.later_quote: despite changes having been made previously the current practices in place for the handover of patients at an Emergency Department far too often results in wholly unacceptable delays with patients being kept waiting for long periods in ambulances and ambulance resources consequently being unavailable for allocation to other calls.

members.title: Lilly Baxandall
members.explanation: Both reports identify that poor handover processes in emergency departments cause prolonged ambulance waits, tying up resources.
members.earlier_quote: the current practices in place for the handover of patients at an Emergency Department far too often results in wholly unacceptable delays with patients being kept waiting for long periods
members.later_quote: concerns regarding the handover of patients at an emergency department which resulted in "unacceptable delays with patients being kept waiting for long periods in ambulances

members.title: Nicola Owens: Prevention of Future Deaths Report
members.explanation: Both reports identify patient handover delays in emergency departments as causing ambulances to be held up and unavailable for other calls.
members.earlier_quote: the current practices in place for the handover of patients at an Emergency Department far too often results in wholly unacceptable delays
members.later_quote: The delay in an ambulance attending patients due to the unavailability of ambulances.

members.title: Roman Barr: Prevention of future deaths report
members.explanation: Both reports identify prolonged ambulance handover times as a cause of delayed patient care and reduced emergency resource availability. The later report reiterates this hazard while adding contextual details about demand periods.
members.earlier_quote: the current practices in place for the handover of patients at an Emergency Department far too often results in wholly unacceptable delays
members.later_quote: Prolonged ambulance handover times at local hospitals were a significant factor in no ambulance being available at the time help was sought

hazard: Lack of clinical observations for 12 hours

anchor.title: Barbara White
anchor.quote: There was a lack of clinical observations for a period of 12 hours on the 9th December. In addition no nursing observations were carried out during this period of time.

members.title: Neil Carter
members.explanation: Both reports highlight insufficient nursing observations as a safety concern. They also note staffing and communication shortcomings contributing to the observation gaps.
members.earlier_quote: lack of clinical observations for a period of 12 hours
members.later_quote: There were repeated failures to perform basic nursing observations

members.title: Agnes Hannan
members.explanation: Both reports highlight failures in maintaining adequate patient records and communication, which can lead to missed clinical information and delayed interventions.
members.earlier_quote: There was a lack of clinical observations for a period of 12 hours on the 9th December.
members.later_quote: There was an actual, or perceived, lack of availability of the hospital notes and records of previous diagnoses and treatments

members.title: David Hughes
members.explanation: Both reports highlight failures in conducting required patient observations at appropriate intervals. The underlying hazard is inadequate monitoring leading to missed clinical deterioration.
members.earlier_quote: There was a lack of clinical observations for a period of 12 hours on the 9th December.
members.later_quote: Level 2 observations were not conducted at the prescribed time intervals and periods of up to two hours lapsed between observations

members.title: Alan Horrocks: Prevention of future deaths report
members.explanation: Both reports describe failures to perform required patient observations and to act on abnormal scores, delaying detection of clinical deterioration.
members.earlier_quote: There was a lack of clinical observations for a period of 12 hours on the 9th December.
members.later_quote: observations were not completed on the ward overnight on 14 March 2025 in accordance with escalation guidance

hazard: Lack of awareness among healthcare professionals about fire risk of emollients

anchor.title: Brian Bicat
anchor.quote: e Health care professionals in both hospital and community setting may not be aware of the potential fire hazard poised by emollient creams which contain a low level of paraffin

members.title: Pauline Allison: Prevention of future deaths report
members.explanation: Both reports identify paraffin‑based emollient creams as a fire hazard due to their flammable ingredients. The later report elaborates on how the residue accumulates on fabrics and how equipment like air mattresses can worsen ignition.
members.earlier_quote: Paraffin based ointments and emollient creams which contain a low level of paraffin pose a potential fire hazard risk
members.later_quote: emollient creams containing flammable ingredients. I heard evidence that these ingredients can build up on clothing and bedding.

members.title: James Rownsley: Prevention of future deaths report
members.explanation: Both reports identify paraffin‑based emollient creams as a fire hazard when exposed to flames or heat. They highlight the need for better awareness and communication about this risk.
members.earlier_quote: Paraffin based ointments and emollient creams which contain a low level of paraffin pose a potential fire hazard risk
members.later_quote: The need for effective communication to partners and stakeholders responsible for either prescribing such emollients, or indeed caring for people in the community, of the dangers of using such creams particularly when in close proximity to flames or heat.

anchor.title: Juan Martin: Prevention of future deaths report
anchor.quote: bed capacity remains an ongoing problem and has not been resolved

members.title: Matthew Sheldrick (1): Prevention of Future Deaths Report
members.explanation: Both reports identify a shortage of mental health inpatient beds as causing excessively long waits in emergency departments. This bed shortage creates a risk of harm to patients awaiting appropriate care.
members.earlier_quote: no suitable bed was identified until approximately after 15:00 on 12 April 2022, which then became unavailable.
members.later_quote: The lack of inpatient beds leading to the unacceptable wait time in A&E for those suffering with their mental health who are awaiting beds.

members.title: Matthew Sheldrick (2): Prevention of Future Deaths Report
members.explanation: Both reports identify insufficient mental‑health inpatient bed provision as creating prolonged emergency department stays for people in crisis.
members.earlier_quote: Witnesses confirmed that no suitable bed was identified until approximately after 15:00 on 12 April 2022, which then became unavailable.
members.later_quote: There is a lack of inpatient beds leading to unacceptable wait times in A&E for those suffering with their mental health who are awaiting beds.

members.title: Martin Bryant: Prevention of future deaths report
members.explanation: Both reports highlight insufficient mental health bed availability leading to prolonged waits for admission.
members.earlier_quote: bed capacity in London remains inadequate.
members.later_quote: The lack of beds, locally and nationally, for mental health admissions and the suggestion given in evidence that patients can be waiting in the open reception area for days or sometimes weeks for a bed.

anchor.title: Sharon Butcher
anchor.quote: There was a 10 minute delay and the prisons local protocol for summoning an ambulance was not followed

members.title: Hayden Norton
members.explanation: Both reports identify a delay in summoning an emergency ambulance due to the absence or non‑use of a proper emergency code/protocol.
members.earlier_quote: There was a 10 minute delay and the prisons local protocol for summoning an ambulance was not followed.
members.later_quote: There was a delay in calling an emergency ambulance because HMP Dartmoor did not have an emergency code (unlike HMP Exeter) protocol.

members.title: John O'Meara
members.explanation: Both reports describe a delay in summoning emergency assistance because prison staff did not follow the established code‑blue/red activation procedure. This failure creates a risk of preventable deaths.
members.earlier_quote: There was a 10 minute delay and the prisons local protocol for summoning an ambulance was not followed.
members.later_quote: | am concerned that Prison Officers are not strictly following the Code Blue/Red system which is meaning there is a delay in the London Ambulance being called.

anchor.title: Liam Lambert
anchor.quote: This ACCT was only open for a short period. It did not serve Liam's needs properly and was closed before any review system picked up the inadequacies.

members.title: Sean Higgins: Prevention of Future Deaths Report
members.explanation: Both reports highlight failures in completing and reviewing required documentation during ACCT assessments, which undermines accurate risk evaluation.
members.earlier_quote: The ACCT document was not completed fully, did not accompany Liam around the prison as it should have
members.later_quote: some officers chairing reviews did not read relevant documentation beyond the last ACCT review prior to the review taking place

members.title: Rickie Poon: Prevention of future deaths report
members.explanation: Both reports identify shortcomings in the ACCT assessment process, such as incomplete documentation and inconsistent supervision during reviews.
members.earlier_quote: The ACCT document was not completed fully, did not accompany Liam around the prison as it should have
members.later_quote: - the ACCT process was not managed and implemented properly, e.g. supervising officers did not consistently acquaint themselves with case notes or history when completing reviews;

anchor.title: Leonard Harmsworth: Prevention of future deaths report
anchor.quote: I remain significantly concerned that delays are continuing and that deaths will continue to occur into the future.

members.title: Jean Frickel: Prevention of future deaths report
members.explanation: Both reports highlight delays in ambulance availability as a safety concern. The earlier report focuses on prolonged response and handover times, while the later report links delays to patient flow bottlenecks caused by social‑care shortages.
members.earlier_quote: Following the fall at home on 7th June 2022 WAST were contacted at 05:23. An ambulance arrived 17 hours 22 minutes later.
members.later_quote: It seems that patient flow i.e. those patients who are ready to be discharged from hospital but are unable to be discharged due to insufficiencies in social care means that ambulances are unable to offload patients into the Emergency Department

members.title: Jeanette Sidlow Beech: Prevention of Future Deaths Report
members.explanation: Both reports highlight prolonged ambulance-related delays—waiting for arrival or handover—that can lead to preventable harm. The underlying hazard is systemic delay in emergency medical response.
members.earlier_quote: On arrival at Ysbyty Glan Clwyd Leonard Harmsworth then waited in the ambulance for 12 hours 4 minutes before being handed over to nursing staff.
members.later_quote: It took a total period of 15 hours and 13 minutes for an ambulance to attend upon Jeanette, by which time she was in cardiac arrest and resuscitation efforts were unsuccessful.

anchor.title: Janet Smith: Prevention of future deaths report
anchor.quote: no carer was in the lounge area monitoring the residents

members.title: Edith Alden: Prevention of future deaths report
members.explanation: Both reports identify inadequate supervision of residents as a key factor contributing to preventable falls. They highlight that insufficient staff presence or unclear responsibilities leave high‑risk individuals unwatched, increasing fall risk.
members.earlier_quote: no carer was in the lounge area monitoring the residents. Accordingly, when Mrs. Smith left the lounge area she was not monitored as required.
members.later_quote: Residents deemed as at very high risk of falls were, and still are, allowed in communal areas with no carer present.

members.title: Patricia Barnett: Prevention of future deaths report
members.explanation: Both reports identify the hazard of residents being left unsupervised in the lounge area, which increases the risk of falls and potential death.
members.earlier_quote: Accordingly, when Mrs. Smith left the lounge area she was not monitored as required.
members.later_quote: I am concerned that Mrs Barnett was left unsupervised in the lounge area.

anchor.title: Carole Lovett
anchor.quote: when the monitoring equipment alarmed this did not result in senior staff attending

members.title: James O'Brien
members.explanation: Both reports highlight shortcomings in staff preparedness and response during patient deterioration. They each point to gaps in training, communication, or familiarity that hindered timely intervention.
members.earlier_quote: The level of competence and training of staff working in the Acute Assessment Unit with regard to the use of NEW Score system and communication between all levels of staff.
members.later_quote: (7) There was a failure to ensure that staff were adequately trained to respond to an emergency situation.

members.title: Robert Lowe
members.explanation: Both reports highlight failures where audible alarms do not lead to appropriate staff response.
members.earlier_quote: when the monitoring equipment alarmed this did not result in senior staff attending.
members.later_quote: important audible alarms may not come to the attention of staff.

anchor.title: Alexander Ball
anchor.quote: There was a lack of communication between the Partnership Trust and other agencies

members.title: Grant Burns
members.explanation: Both reports identify insufficient communication among involved agencies as a contributing factor. The later report specifies the agencies involved while the earlier notes a missing care‑coordinator role.
members.earlier_quote: There was a lack of communication between the Partnership Trust and other agencies.
members.later_quote: (3) There was a lack of communication between partner agencies

members.title: Mark McKessy: Prevention of future deaths report
members.explanation: Both reports highlight inadequate communication and information sharing among agencies leading to fragmented care. The later report adds concerns about unrecognised health needs but centres on the same coordination failure.
members.earlier_quote: There was a lack of communication between the Partnership Trust and other agencies.
members.later_quote: Poor communication/information sharing between agencies which meant that there was no coordination of care
